description: runoutSIM is an R package from Jason Goetz and collaborators for regional landslide runout and connectivity calculations. It combines random-walk routing with the Perla two-parameter friction model and provides tools for parameter searches and parallel execution. Inputs include a terrain raster, source locations and optional receiving features such as roads or rivers. Spatial coverage and cell size follow the user domain; the own tutorial uses a 12.5-metre terrain grid and 73 mapped runouts in the Rio Olivares basin in Chile. Its results can support screening of infrastructure exposure and landslide connections to river networks. The code and version 1.0 archive are free under MIT, with sf and terra used for spatial objects. A limitation is that the tutorial requires a projected UTM coordinate system and appropriately prepared terrain. The example inventory does not establish performance for every landslide process or region. No directly related catalogue record was found. Documentation and file identities were inspected without downloading the example rasters or running R.
